 View Comments Metro Weather Politics Sports Business Puzzles Rhode Island Globe Magazine Opinion Health care Arts Lifestyle Education Cambridge & Somerville Money, Power, Inequality Spotlight Technology Climate Cars Real Estate Events On Basketball The Celtics believe they have a good team, but will it be good enough to compete with the elite of the Eastern Conference?
 Print this Article 
 View Comments Coach Joe Mazzulla on his Celtics: “I love this team. I love who we can become.” Barry Chin/Globe Staff DETROIT — The one coherent theme emanating from Celtics training camp and the post-Jaylen Brown era is that the franchise feels comfortable and confident in the team it will field this season. 
 With Brown on to Philadelphia, replaced by 36-year-old Paul George , and Jayson Tatum healthy and ready to reassume his status as a top-five NBA player, the Celtics enter the season as an overshadowed entity — a team that has the potential to emerge among the elite teams in the Eastern Conference but carries a plethora of unknowns and question marks that will take time to resolve. 
 Tuesday’s afternoon opener at Detroit will be the first opportunity for the Celtics to unleash a roster brimming with potential, depth, and the ability to defend tenaciously. The East is difficult and balanced. With the new antitanking rules implemented to prevent teams from purposely losing to gain a premium draft pick, there will be no easy trips to Brooklyn, Washington, or Indiana. 
 Get Court Sense Keep up with everything Celtics with news, commentary, and analysis from the Globe's all-star team. Arrives twice weekly. Enter Email Sign Up The Celtics may not match last season’s 56-win total, but the emphasis has changed from previous years. The franchise realizes that perhaps too much emphasis was placed on the regular season and not enough on sustainability in the postseason. 
 This new approach will rely on depth, increased offensive versatility, and ball movement. The presence of Mitchell Robinson in the paint should enhance the defense and give the Celtics more offensive possessions. The hope is that George not only stays healthy but can provide complementary production on both sides of the ball, a spot-up shooting element the Celtics have missed the past few years. 
 The Celtics will hope veteran Paul George can make a significant impact on both sides of the ball. Barry Chin/Globe Staff After a month of watching his revamped team — how well it worked together, how hard it has played, and the steps many young players have taken forward — coach Joe Mazzulla feels confident about its potential. 
 “I do love this team,” he said. “I do want to see who we are when it doesn’t go our way. I want to say, ‘OK, I love our team but what are we going to be after a winning streak, after a losing streak, after four games in five nights?’ All those things. 
 “I love this team. I love who we can become, but I also am excited to go through all the [expletive] that the NBA season gives you. I’m excited to lose with this team. I’m excited to win with this team. I’m excited to do all those things to see who we become on the other side of it.” 
 The Pistons should provide a hardy opening test, having just re-signed hulking center Jalen Duren, who will provide major resistance to Robinson and Neemias Queta. Cade Cunningham returns for another season as the franchise cornerstone, while Ausar Thompson is one of the league’s top defenders. 
 Related : The Globe's predictions for the 2026-27 NBA season Detroit finished last season as the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference, but inexperience and the inability to find a secondary scorer to Cunningham in clutch moments were its downfall. The Pistons lost Tobias Harris and Caris LeVert in the offseason but added athletic big man John Collins along with sharpshooter Isaiah Joe and veteran Taurean Prince. 
 The Pistons are the beginning of what will be a challenging early schedule for the Celtics that takes them on the road for 13 of their first 21 games, including matchups with the Knicks, Magic, Rockets, 76ers, Raptors, Mavericks (twice), Nuggets, Warriors, Hawks, and Spurs. 
 Because of the increased competitiveness in the NBA, the Celtics could actually be a better team than last season’s 56-win product but win fewer games. The focus of training camp was for teammates to galvanize and get accustomed to new roles. 
 For the first time in his career, Tatum is the unquestioned No. 1 option, and he enters the season among the top 10 MVP candidates. The Celtics may need a better-than-ever Tatum to compete with the likes of the Knicks, 76ers, Pistons, and Cavaliers in the East. 
 Related : Globe’s Celtics writers discuss key story lines, give their thoughts on the coming NBA season in Boston “Obviously, JT is the guy,” George said . “And I only want to make this game is as easy as possible for him, while not having him put that burden or pressure that he has to perform. Obviously we need him to perform at a high level every night, but the expectation that he has to or we don’t have a chance is kind of to alleviate that pressure off of him.” 
 This team will be fascinating to watch because of its potential and reliance on players such as Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman, Jordan Walsh, and even Ron Harper Jr. to improve and become consistent contributors. The plan is for the Celtics to batter teams with their energy and depth, to surround Robinson with shooters, and to spread the contribution responsibility. 
 Of course, that means Derrick White, recently extended Payton Pritchard , and Sam Hauser will have to improve their 3-point consistency. But the Celtics should be tougher to guard than in years past because of their bevy of shooters, and they should be better defensively and on the boards. But the quandary is the rest of the East is better too, with the likes of Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kawhi Leonard, and LeBron James joining teams with the express purpose of reaching the Finals, so this could be Mazzulla’s biggest challenge yet. It will be an enthralling ride, for sure.
